newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador exports rise through Febraury.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador exports rise through Febraury.

text.p: Exports in El Salvador totalled $396 million for the first two months of the year, an increase of 21 percent over the same period in 1996, the Central Reserve Bank said on Monday.
Imports also rose in January and February, reaching 567 million, up 17 percent over the first two months of 1996.
The trade deficit in El Salvador during January and Feburary was $171 million, some $5 million less than during the same period a year ago.
"The increase (in exports) is explained by ... traditional exports, which reached $135 million," an increase of $36 million, the Central Reserve Bank said in a report.
Coffee accounted for $118 million of the traditional export total.
Non-traditional exports, led by medicines, processed food products and aluminium, generated $109 million, the report said.
The remaining $152 million came from textile exports, which were up 32 percent over the first two months of 1996, the report said.
